newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says Paris, Bonn want punctual EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says Paris, Bonn want punctual EMU start.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Thursday both Paris and Bonn were in agreement that Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) should begin on time and in compliance with the convergence criteria.

Speaking to journalists at a joint news conference with French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine, Kinkel said: "My French colleague can speak for himself, but I think I can say we both want the start to begin as laid down in the (Maastricht) treaty and according to the convergence criteria."
Kinkel and Vedrine had spent the afternoon together discussing the proposed single European currency as well as next week's NATO's Madrid summit on eastern European expansion.
Earlier Kinkel and Vedrine had ridden bicycles along the banks of the Rhine river to try to show that the Bonn-Paris tandem at the heart of European integration was still in good working order.
"I think we have given you a good image. We cycled together in the same direction," Vedrine, who earlier held talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, told reporters on the river bank.

The Franco-German axis is perceived to be under strain since the election of France's Socialist-led government. The ministers had the task of presenting a united front after French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said that France's public deficit could be "significantly higher" than 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
